name: livesvc-medlink-vault-postgres-access-model
instr:
Only phase 0 of Medlink's Vault and PostgreSQL setup made it into Terraform, and the hand-built rest has drifted. Any PostgreSQL login can read the prod billing tables, the pre-Vault logins `portal_app` and `etl_reader` still work, and decommissioned fax-gateway's AppRole roles still carry `apps-read-all`, which can read every application secret.

To close this out:

- CI's single `terraform apply` of `/workspace/platform` against today's production (live services plus the phase-0 state) must bring everything in `ACCESS_MODEL.md` to exactly what it says, down to the database credentials Vault issues and what people get at login, and leave a clean next plan.
- The configuration must manage everything the model defines: adopt what exists, create what's missing, delete what it retires. Only the configuration ships; state commands and hand edits don't.
- `inventory.auto.tfvars.json` keeps changing: teams, members, schemas and workloads come and go, workloads gain or drop environments, and access, owners and lifetimes change, under any names. Each time, the same configuration must apply in one run, leave a clean plan and change exactly what the model implies.
- Leave `versions.tf`, `providers.tf`, `backend.tf`, `variables.tf` and the inventory alone. Use only the pinned providers' data sources, local modules and these resource types: `postgresql_database`, `postgresql_default_privileges`, `postgresql_extension`, `postgresql_grant`, `postgresql_grant_role`, `postgresql_role`, `post
